result_summary: Held runtime-observed true-edge recall at 0.85 and static marginal true-edge recall at 0.90 while varying conditional complement coverage P(static hit | runtime miss). The same marginals produced materially different union closure safety and throughput: correlated blind spots left substantial stale descendants, while perfect complement eliminated stale state and preserved enough independent work to slightly exceed whole-redraw correct-endpoint throughput in this synthetic DAG. Therefore provenance diversity should be priced by joint miss/complement coverage, not mechanism count or marginal recall alone. A preliminary held-out router pilot was explicitly quarantined and not promoted because its context split used process-local Python hash() and was not reproducible across interpreter starts.
scope: Synthetic mechanism evidence only; no production LLM thresholds or universal q cutoff claimed. Public sources were used only as architecture/background cross-checks.
exact_next_action: On the next invocation resolve and freeze latest sanitized control, then use repository chronology to select the newest own immutable checkpoint. Rebuild the rollback router with a persisted deterministic context manifest, compare marginal-only versus joint-miss-aware routing on held-out fanout/depth/cost/overlap distributions under matched calls, replace oracle closure confidence with explicit proved_new_version/known_uncaptured/unknown states, and build a small public LangGraph provenance-coverage suite measuring descendant closure recall and precision.
